text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The plan matches the code. notifications/sms.py confirms queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) is the only sending path, appends irreversibly to outbox/sms.jsonl, and delivery_status() maps SMS ids to 'delivered'/'failed' with new messages absent. data/sms_status.json shows exactly the 10 failed ids listed (SMS-00001/04/05/06/09/10/12/18/19/20), and the outbox shows each failed message's household_id, template_id and params are stored on its line, so re-queueing with the original template_id/params reproduces the same text. Each failed message belongs to a distinct household, so the per-household dedup set does not drop anyone and matches the ticket's 'exactly one new text per household'. The scripts/stock_report.py pattern (sys.path.insert of repo root, docstring disclosing that it sends SMS) is correctly followed, and the plan correctly avoids touching the outbox directly."}}
reasoning:
The plan step: iterate sent_messages(), for each SmsMessage whose id is in failed set, re-queue via queue_sms(message.household_id, message.template_id, message.params). Dedup per household. This matches the code. Failed ids match R3. Each failed message has a distinct household, so dedup doesn't drop anyone. Docstring requirement: must state it sends SMS — plan says include docstring stating that. sys.path insert matches. All correct.

One nuance: dedup per household — ticket says "every household whose text failed gets exactly one new text". If a household had two failed messages, dedup would give one text, but ticket says exactly one new text per household — dedup aligns with ticket. Fine.

Accept.
